Six years ago, crypto felt like stepping into the wild. No clear paths. No real rules. Just endless possibilities and a whole lot of risk.

Some people charged right in, ready to make their mark. Most? They didn’t know where to start. That’s where Quidax came in.

‍

It was the guide at the gate, the friendly face showing people how to take their first steps into this new world. Quidax made crypto feel like a place where any beginner could trade without feeling out of place. And for a while, that was enough. Until it wasn’t.

‍

Because rookies don’t stay rookies forever. They get sharper. They take bolder risks. They stop testing the waters and start chasing bigger tides. Quidax had built a loyal following, but it had also built something else - a tribe of traders who had outgrown their first steps. Yet, the brand still spoke to them as if they were just starting.

‍

The market saw Quidax as a stepping stone, a safe harbour for beginners before they set sail for deeper waters. But Quidax wasn’t a harbour anymore. It was a vessel. And it was time to build the kind of ship that could weather the storms of serious trade.
From Campfire Lessons to Mountain Quests

There’s a misconception that simplicity and depth can’t exist in the same breath. That a platform built to be accessible must, by default, lack the weight, the infrastructure, the sheer force needed to handle high-stakes, high-volume transactions.

‍

That was the perception Quidax had to dismantle.

‍

Because beneath the surface, the platform had already evolved. It was no longer just for those making their first trade. It was home to full-time traders, market tacticians, and digital asset navigators who charted their own courses, wielding data like a map and volatility like a challenge.

‍

And yet, Quidax was still seen as a starter pack, not the full gear haul it had become.

‍

If perception is reality, then reality needed rewriting.

Quidax didn’t just need a new coat of paint. It needed to be seen for what it had become: a full-scale exchange where every trader, at every stage, had the tools to win.

‍

And so, the story shifted.

‍

Quidax wasn’t just a platform anymore. It became an expedition. A treasure hunt. A place where fortune favours the bold, where each trade was a move on the map, where the most daring didn’t just play the game - they changed it.

‍

At the heart of it all was one guiding concept statement: The Adventure of Relentless Fortune Seekers. Not just a tagline or a campaign, but the core belief driving every design choice, every word, every partnership principle and space system. Quidax wasn’t just for those curious about crypto - it was for those restless enough to chase it down.

‍

The entire language of the brand followed suit. This wasn’t about “buying and selling crypto.” That was too dry, too static, too lifeless for an industry built on movement. Instead, we invited traders to embark, to discover, to uncover hidden opportunities in a market that never stood still.

‍

Quidax had been a bridge. Now, it was a launchpad.
A Universe of Fortune and Fire

With a new narrative came a new visual world, one that pulsed with the urgency of ambition and the promise of discovery. Gemstones became the cornerstone, a motif of hidden wealth waiting to be unearthed. The colour palette deepened into a realm of electric blues, purples, and streaks of neon, a visual language that spoke in the hues of movement, ambition, and high-stakes exploration.

‍

But a brand is only as strong as those who champion it.

‍

And so, the world of Quidax expanded beyond the platform itself. The partnerships had to match the energy, the hunger, the audacity of the traders who called Quidax home. This wasn’t a brand for the passive, the cautious, the ones content with watching from the sidelines.

‍

It was for the risk-takers, the high-velocity decision-makers, the ones who thrive on volatility.

‍

Extreme sports athletes. High-stakes crypto analysts. Digital pioneers who don’t just navigate the chaos - they make it their own.

‍

We didn’t just change how Quidax speaks. We changed who speaks for it.

The shift wasn’t subtle or small. It was tectonic.

‍

The platform once known as a safe place for beginners now stood as a full-fledged canyon for traders who had no interest in playing it safe. The brand, once perceived as a launchpad for newcomers, was now the playground where seasoned traders honed their edge.

‍

No more hesitation. No more underestimation. No more mistaking simplicity for smallness.

‍

This was Quidax, built for the seekers, the risk-takers, the ones who don’t wait for the future but claim it, trade by trade.

‍

And the quest has only just begun.

A Simple Approach To Financial Accessibility

Access to poor financial services plagues several African communities. In Nigeria, however, electronic payments have been growing at a rate of 15% annually, with an explosive $320 billion worth of transactions conducted in 2018 alone.

Solutions like POS systems, mobile money, and online merchant payments—all introduced to improve financial accessibility—are promoting this growth. And Kele, with its versatile digital prowess, isn't merely planning to be a part of this ensemble—they’re setting up to lead the whole industry.

‍

At its core, Kele is more than just a digital wallet. It's an ecosystem that supports both banked and unbanked customers, delivering a range of services right from P2P transfers and airtime purchases to complex betting code generations and utility payments.

‍

While many e-wallets cater to specific niches, Kele's vision is expansive. Beyond standard wallet services, its association with BetKing's Agent Network allows excellent synergy - bringing the unbanked into the financial fold, fueled by a vast network of over 19,000 agents and 3.2 million+ walk-in users. And that's just the beginning. Their entry strategy, grounded in BetKing's existing network, promises to expand their footprint exponentially.

‍
Establishing Kele as a Market Leader

Working on impact-focused projects is core to our existence, so when Kele approached us to craft a brand identity and mobile app echoing their mission of powering financial freedom in Africa, partnering with them was a no-brainer. 

‍

Kele aims to stand out in Nigeria's bustling digital wallet scene, so it needed an identity and product experience that would declare to every Nigerian, 'Delete the 25 other fintech apps on your phone. Kele is all you need.

First, we delved deep into discussions with the Kele team to understand what experiences they prioritised most in delivering financial inclusion. We also wanted to understand the values that drove their passion and their plans for eventually bridging the financial divide. 

‍

A key determinant of our strategy was that Kele wanted to build an application that was easy for anyone to use, regardless of age or level of education. Accessibility and convenience were our guiding compass.

Reimagining the Wallet

One of Kele’s core offerings inspired us: “Digital Wallet for Seamless Payment Experiences.” Inspired by this, we designed a logo inspired by an open wallet and the letter ‘K,’ making their commitment to seamlessness and convenience a key part of their brand.

‍

We also used bright colours—blues, greens, and oranges—to help Kele’s brand be perceived as fun, approachable, and perfect for daily use.

Smooth and Seamless Transactions

The visual language for Kele’s brand and app will help keep things fresh and simple for the everyday man. For the mobile app, we optimised for scalability, simplicity, convenience, security, and speed—all of which are core to achieving delightful user experiences.

Kele's vision to spearhead financial inclusivity has taken a concrete shape post-launch, signaling the dawn of a new era in the Nigerian fintech landscape. Users have expressed appreciation for Kele's tangible difference in their daily transactions, from P2P transfers to utility payments, all within a few taps on their mobile devices. Through strategic brand positioning and a focus on user-centric design, Kele has established a strong foundation for growth. As it continues to build on this momentum, Kele is not just a participant in Nigeria's digital payment space but is becoming synonymous with the ease and freedom of modern financial services.

Harnessing the power of community to propel the future of work
Brand Strategy, Communications Design, Website Design
Propel empowers the global workforce by building ecosystem infrastructure to connect African talent to global opportunities.

Founded initially as Hirefreehands, they focused on connecting global companies with African remote talent.
However, Propel soon realized the limits of this model. This led to an audacious pivot to build a support ecosystem for communities and their members. Through strengthening communities, they are reimagining a future where work is genuinely borderless and everyone has equal access to global opportunities.

Propel needed to stand out in a highly competitive market dominated by giants like Indeed, Deel, and Toptal. While most of its competitors have a core focus on talent matching, Propel is taking a different approach by nurturing the entire ecosystem that produces talent. They needed a strategy that correctly encapsulated this unique positioning.
Over the coming weeks, we had discovery sessions with the Propel team. To transform their business, we needed to walk in their shoes and understand their business needs.

First, A Great Name For Take-off

‍

The Hirefreehands name no longer reflected Propel's identity. Considering their new mission, defining their audience, and testing different iterations, the name ‘Propel’ was unearthed.

‍

            Propel /prəˈpel/. Take-off, Elevate, Push Limits, Unending Possibilities.

‍

Stepping on Stacked Bricks to Access Opportunity

‍

With community at the center, we made the Propel logomark to reflect their goals. We created an abstract illustration of “Stacked Bricks” which literally implies building and metaphorically represents the Propel brand promise to be the reliable bridge between communities, their talent, and the best global opportunities.

‍

In The Propelverse Lies The Key

‍

We overhauled the previous visual identity and created an entire universe to perfectly capture the new visual system defined for Propel. This ranged from colours to typography, brand patterns, illustrations, iconography, and imagery direction.

We intentionally created bold, authentic, future-centric, and exploratory brand elements, which are the core attributes of Propel’s personality. We carefully merged this personality with a tone and voice that resonates with their target audience -  people and companies seeking growth.

Expanding the borders for Africa’s $60 billion creator economy
Selar had outgrown the old idea of a creator

In the rise of independent digital entrepreneurship, Selar had earned strong recognition as the e-commerce platform for creators, people who knew they had something to sell, teach, package, or distribute online. 

‍

As the creator economy matured, the category around it started to feel too narrow for the opportunity ahead.

‍

“Creator” had begun to harden into a familiar type: the influencer, the educator, the content professional, the digital entrepreneur who already knew how to name what they were building.Yet across Africa, there were far more people sitting just outside that definition, people with useful knowledge, lived experience, practical skills, niche passions, or cultural perspectives that could be turned into value, but who did not yet see themselves reflected in the language of the category.

‍
Selar no longer had to communicate from inside a narrow creator archetype. It could now stand for a broader and more inclusive truth about the economy taking shape around it.
We rebuilt the platform around a more democratic idea of creation

Our work began with a bigger belief which we crystallized into a new tagline, “Everyone Has Something”. Not everyone has an audience yet.

‍

Not everyone has polished content, a refined product, or the confidence to call themselves a creator. But almost everyone has something, something they know, something they make, something they have learned, something they care about, something another person might find useful, meaningful, or worth paying for.

‍

That idea became the organising principle for the new identity system we built.

‍

It helped move Selar away from sounding like a platform built only for the already-converted, and toward sounding like a platform for people at many different points of creative possibility. It made the brand warmer, wider, and more culturally expansive without making it vague.

‍
Launching a new era of growth

What changed was not just the feel of the brand, but the size of the world it could credibly speak to. 

Selar no longer had to communicate from inside a narrow creator archetype. It could now stand for a broader and more inclusive truth about the economy taking shape around it, that creativity is not the preserve of a small digital class, but a wider human possibility. The platform upon which we rebuilt the brand got the business more aligned with the scale of participation the creator economy was already increasingly demanding, helping Selar claim a larger, more consequential role in the future of creative independence across Africa.

…but that opportunity came with risk. In a category shaped by importation, scepticism, and the memory of past industrial exits,
BUP had to build confidence early and convincingly, long before the product itself could do the talking.

Building a living proof point for a future in the making

We did that by building a digital experience that opened up the anatomy of a BUP tyre, showing how every layer, from rubber compound to geometry, contributed to performance.

Repositioning a 36-year giant for the future of energy
Repositioning a 36-year giant for the future of energy
The world was changing its mind about energy

At a time when the global commercial value of oil and gas was under pressure and the world was accelerating toward renewable energy, NLNG recognised that its future could not rest on legacy relevance alone.

It needed to position itself more sustainably for the future of energy, not only as a company with history and scale, but as one with direction, adaptability, and a clearer place in a changing global landscape.
That shift was made more urgent by a second challenge closer to home.

In Nigeria, NLNG was still often misunderstood as being fully government-owned.  For a business trying to step into a broader and more future-facing role, that misconception made it harder for the company to be engaged at the level it now needed to occupy.
We gave NLNG a stronger way to be encountered not as a static legacy institution explaining itself, but as a dynamic energy company actively shaping where it is going.
Painting a new picture fit for the future
NLNG partnered with us to give that strategic shift a compelling form the world could actually experience.

Their website was the clearest public stage on which NLNG’s next chapter could begin to speak for itself, so it had to do far more than update appearance or improve navigation. It had to help the company leave behind an older reading of itself and enter a more expansive one.

Built around NLNG’s new brand essence as a global energy company in motion improving lives sustainably, we redesigned NLNG’s website to communicate a business no longer content to be understood only through inherited assumptions about oil, gas, or state proximity.

Through a more immersive visual system, a clearer narrative structure, and a more contemporary way of organising the company’s story, we helped NLNG translate its evolved industrial credibility into a public language fit for the future. We gave the giant a stronger way to be encountered not as a static legacy institution explaining itself, but as a dynamic energy company actively shaping where it is going.
Gaining a signal equal to stature
What changed was not simply the polish of NLNG’s website, but the level at which NLNG could now be understood.

The new website and repositioning gave the business a more credible public face for a new era, one better suited to the expectations of partners, stakeholders, vendors, and audiences looking for signs of seriousness, adaptability, and direction in a changing energy market.
